questions.question: Explain the eight limbs of Raja Yoga as per Patanjali’s Yoga Sutras.
questions.solution_html:
• The Eight Limbs of Raja Yoga (Patanjali's Yoga Sutras)
  • ● Yama (Restraints): Ethical guidelines for interactions with others and oneself.
  • ● Niyama (Observances): Personal disciplines and practices.
  • ● Asana (Postures): Physical postures, a foundational aspect of yoga practice.
  • ● Pranayama (Breath Control): Techniques to regulate and control the breath.
  • ● Pratyahara (Withdrawal of the Senses): Turning inward and controlling the senses.
  • ● Dharana : Focusing the mind on a single point.
  • ● Dhyana (Meditation): Sustained, focused concentration and mindfulness.
  • ● Samadhi (Union/Absorption): A state of deep absorption and union with the Self.
questions.final_answer: ● Samadhi (Union/Absorption): A state of deep absorption and union with the Self

questions.question: What is Yoga? Provide a brief explanation of its origins. Yoga is a spiritual discipline rooted
questions.solution_html:
• in ancient Indian philosophy. It is both a science and an art of healthy living, aimed at bringing
  • harmony between the body, mind, and spirit. The word Yoga comes from the Sanskrit root "Yuj"
  • which means "to join" or "to unite." According to Yogic scriptures, this union is the merging of
  • individual consciousness with universal consciousness, resulting in a state of perfect balance and
  • liberation known as moksha or kaivalya. Yoga encompasses various methods such as physical
  • postures (asanas), breathing techniques (pranayama), meditation, and ethical disciplines to
  • achieve self-realization and freedom from suffering.
  • Origins and Historical Development
questions.final_answer: Origins and Historical Development

questions.question: Discuss about yoga prayer.
questions.solution_html:
• Prayers in yoga play a vital role in setting the tone for the practice. They create a sacred, mindful
  • environment and help practitioners connect to the tradition and purpose of yoga. The opening
  • prayer typically focuses on cultivating focus, respect for the practice, and unity among
  • practitioners, while the closing prayer fosters gratitude, peace, and reflection on the practice.
  • Opening Prayer (Sanskrit with Meaning)
  • Sanskrit
  • Om Saha Navavatu
  • Saha Nau Bhunaktu
  • Saha Viryam Karavavahai
  • Tejasvi Navadhitamastu Ma Vidvishavahai
  • Om Shanti Shanti Shantiḥ
  • Meaning
  • ● May we be protected together.
  • ● May we be nourished together.
  • ● May we work together with great energy.
  • ● May our knowledge be illuminating and fruitful.
  • ● May we live in harmony and peace.
  • Closing Prayer (Sanskrit with Meaning)
  • Sanskrit
  • Om Asato Ma Sad Gamaya
  • Tamaso Ma Jyotir Gamaya
  • Mrityor Ma Amritam Gamaya
  • Om Shanti Shanti Shantiḥ
  • Meaning
  • ● Lead me from untruth to truth.
  • ● Lead me from darkness to light.
  • ● Lead me from death to immortality.
  • ● Let there be peace, peace, peace.
questions.final_answer: ● Let there be peace, peace, peace

questions.question: Explain the eight limbs of Raja Yoga as per Patanjali’s Yoga Sutras.
questions.solution_html:
• The Eight Limbs of Raja Yoga (Patanjali's Yoga Sutras)
  • ● Yama (Restraints): Ethical guidelines for interactions with others and oneself.
  • ● Niyama (Observances): Personal disciplines and practices.
  • ● Asana (Postures): Physical postures, a foundational aspect of yoga practice.
  • ● Pranayama (Breath Control): Techniques to regulate and control the breath.
  • ● Pratyahara (Withdrawal of the Senses): Turning inward and controlling the senses.
  • ● Dharana : Focusing the mind on a single point.
  • ● Dhyana (Meditation): Sustained, focused concentration and mindfulness.
  • ● Samadhi (Union/Absorption): A state of deep absorption and union with the Self.
questions.final_answer: ● Samadhi (Union/Absorption): A state of deep absorption and union with the Self

questions.question: What is Yoga? Provide a brief explanation of its origins. Yoga is a spiritual discipline rooted
questions.solution_html:
• in ancient Indian philosophy. It is both a science and an art of healthy living, aimed at bringing
  • harmony between the body, mind, and spirit. The word Yoga comes from the Sanskrit root "Yuj"
  • which means "to join" or "to unite." According to Yogic scriptures, this union is the merging of
  • individual consciousness with universal consciousness, resulting in a state of perfect balance and
  • liberation known as moksha or kaivalya. Yoga encompasses various methods such as physical
  • postures (asanas), breathing techniques (pranayama), meditation, and ethical disciplines to
  • achieve self-realization and freedom from suffering.
  • Origins and Historical Development
questions.final_answer: Origins and Historical Development

questions.question: Discuss about yoga prayer.
questions.solution_html:
• Prayers in yoga play a vital role in setting the tone for the practice. They create a sacred, mindful
  • environment and help practitioners connect to the tradition and purpose of yoga. The opening
  • prayer typically focuses on cultivating focus, respect for the practice, and unity among
  • practitioners, while the closing prayer fosters gratitude, peace, and reflection on the practice.
  • Opening Prayer (Sanskrit with Meaning)
  • Sanskrit
  • Om Saha Navavatu
  • Saha Nau Bhunaktu
  • Saha Viryam Karavavahai
  • Tejasvi Navadhitamastu Ma Vidvishavahai
  • Om Shanti Shanti Shantiḥ
  • Meaning
  • ● May we be protected together.
  • ● May we be nourished together.
  • ● May we work together with great energy.
  • ● May our knowledge be illuminating and fruitful.
  • ● May we live in harmony and peace.
  • Closing Prayer (Sanskrit with Meaning)
  • Sanskrit
  • Om Asato Ma Sad Gamaya
  • Tamaso Ma Jyotir Gamaya
  • Mrityor Ma Amritam Gamaya
  • Om Shanti Shanti Shantiḥ
  • Meaning
  • ● Lead me from untruth to truth.
  • ● Lead me from darkness to light.
  • ● Lead me from death to immortality.
  • ● Let there be peace, peace, peace.
questions.final_answer: ● Let there be peace, peace, peace
